events.name: Jemdet Nasr settlement becomes a regional centre near Kish
events.description: The type site of the Jemdet Nasr period grows into a regional centre, giving its name to the culture that closes the Uruk era in southern Mesopotamia.

events.name: Numerical clay tablets spread across Mesopotamia
events.description: Geometric numerical tablets and archaic pictographic records are used for accounting across settlements between the rivers, on the eve of cuneiform writing.

events.name: The Awan dynasty briefly holds the kingship of Sumer
events.description: An Elamite dynasty from the region of Awan is listed among the holders of the kingship of Sumer in the Sumerian King List.

events.name: Hadanish rules Hamazi as a power between Kish and Nippur
events.description: Hadanish, the ruler recorded for Hamazi in the Sumerian King List, governs a city-state counted among the great cities of Sumer before the Akkadian conquest.

events.name: Susuda takes the kingship of Kish
events.description: Susuda founds the second dynasty of Kish, one of the dynasties listed between the first dynasty of Ur and the dynasty of Awan in the Sumerian King List.

events.name: The Second Dynasty of Ur rules the city of Ur
events.description: Two kings — Nanni and his son Mesh-ki-ang-Nanna — are recorded for the second dynasty of Ur in the Sumerian King List. Conventional dates for this dynasty are disputed.

events.name: The Third Dynasty of Kish, dynasty of Kubaba
events.description: The third dynasty of Kish is recorded in the Sumerian King List; its most notable ruler is Kubaba, the only woman listed as holder of the kingship of Kish.

events.name: Shu-Suen, last ruler listed for Akshak
events.description: Shu-Suen is the last king recorded for the dynasty of Akshak in the Sumerian King List, before the kingship passes to the fourth dynasty of Kish.

events.name: Zimudar takes the kingship of Kish
events.description: Zimudar founds the fourth dynasty of Kish, recorded in the Sumerian King List alongside Usi-watar, Eshtar-muti, Ishme-Shamash, Nanniya and Puzur-Suen.

events.name: The Fourth Dynasty of Uruk rules Uruk after the Gutian period
events.description: Ur-nigin, Ur-gigir, Kuda, Puzur-ili and Ur-Utu are recorded as the fourth dynasty of Uruk in the Sumerian King List; conventional dates for this dynasty are disputed.

events.name: Sharrum-iter takes the kingship of Mari
events.description: Sharrum-iter founds the dynasty of Mari, the first ruler recorded for the city in the Sumerian King List.

events.name: Reign of Peshgaldaramesh of the Sealand dynasty
events.description: Peshgaldaramesh takes the throne of the Sealand dynasty, an independent power in southern Mesopotamia contemporary with the later Kassite kings of Babylon.

events.name: Simbar-shipak seizes the throne of Babylon
events.description: Simbar-shipak, a priest from Bit-Dagan, seizes the Babylonian throne and founds the second Sea Land dynasty after the fall of Kassite power.

events.name: Eulmash-shakin-shumi takes the throne of Babylon
events.description: Eulmash-shakin-shumi takes the Babylonian throne, beginning the short Bazi dynasty recorded in the Babylonian King List.

events.name: Mar-biti-apla-usur founds the Elamite dynasty of Babylon
events.description: Mar-biti-apla-usur takes the Babylonian throne, founding the five-year Elamite dynasty of the Babylonian King List.

events.name: Nabu-mukin-apli takes the throne of Babylon
events.description: Nabu-mukin-apli founds the dynasty that rules Babylon for over two centuries as Assyrian influence grows in the west.

events.name: Nabu-apla-iddina restores the cult of Shamash at Sippar
events.description: Nabu-apla-iddina restores the cult of the sun-god Shamash at Sippar, commemorated by the famous terracotta plaque showing the seated sun-god.

events.name: Nabopolassar becomes king of Babylon
events.description: Nabopolassar takes the Babylonian throne and throws off Assyrian rule, founding the Chaldean dynasty.

events.name: Nebuchadnezzar II succeeds his father
events.description: Nebuchadnezzar II succeeds Nabopolassar as king of Babylon after the victory over the Egyptians at Carchemish.

events.name: Thutmose III defeats the Mitanni at the Euphrates
events.description: After his victory at Megiddo, Thutmose III crosses the Euphrates and campaigns against Mitanni, the Hurrian kingdom dominating northern Mesopotamia.

events.name: Washukanni becomes the capital of Mitanni
events.description: Washukanni rises as the royal capital of the Mitanni kingdom, later destroyed by Shupiluliuma I of the Hittites.

events.name: Ashur-uballit I makes Assyria a great power
events.description: Ashur-uballit I breaks Mitanni supremacy, Corresponds with the pharaoh as an equal and turns Assyria into a major power of the Late Bronze Age.

events.name: Tukulti-Ninurta I founds Kar-Tukulti-Ninurta
events.description: Tukulti-Ninurta I founds his new royal capital across the Tigris from Ashur after capturing Babylon.

events.name: Gandash founds the Kassite dynasty of Babylon
events.description: Gandash takes control of Babylon, beginning the longest-ruling dynasty in Babylonian history.

events.name: Kurigalzu I builds Dur-Kurigalzu
events.description: Kurigalzu I founds Dur-Kurigalzu as a Kassite royal residence on the Diyala, later excavated with royal tombs and archives.

events.name: Ugarit is destroyed in the final Bronze Age collapse
events.description: The port city of Ugarit is burned and never resettled; its last tablet reports enemy ships and fire in the city.

events.name: The Sea Peoples raid the Egyptian coast
events.description: Ramesses III repels an attack of the Sea Peoples by land and sea, recorded in reliefs at Medinet Habu, amid the wider Bronze Age collapse.

events.name: Nebuchadnezzar II destroys Jerusalem
events.description: Babylonian forces sack Jerusalem and destroy the Temple, beginning the Babylonian Captivity of the Judahites.

events.name: The Ishtar Gate of Babylon is completed
events.description: Nebuchadnezzar II completes the Ishtar Gate, faced with glazed blue bricks and dragons of Marduk, leading into Babylon.

events.name: Cyrus the Great captures Babylon
events.description: Cyrus the Great takes Babylon without a siege of the city itself, ending the Neo-Babylonian Empire and founding the Persian Achaemenid Empire.

events.name: Cambyses II conquers Egypt
events.description: Cambyses II defeats Psamtik III and adds Egypt to the Achaemenid Empire.

events.name: Darius I builds Persepolis
events.description: Darius I begins building Persepolis as the ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Empire.

events.name: Darius I organizes the satrapies of the empire
events.description: Darius I divides the empire into satrapies with regular taxation and the Royal Road, as described by Herodotus.

events.name: Alexander defeats Darius III at Issus
events.description: Alexander the Great routs Darius III at Issus, opening the way to Syria, Egypt and Mesopotamia.

events.name: Alexander the Great enters Babylon
events.description: After the victory at Gaugamela, Alexander enters Babylon and is received as king in the ancient capital.

events.name: Death of Alexander the Great in Babylon
events.description: Alexander dies in Babylon at the age of 32; his empire is soon divided among the Diadochi.

events.name: Seleucus I founds Seleucia on the Tigris
events.description: Seleucus I founds Seleucia on the Tigris as the new capital of the Seleucid Empire, drawing population from Babylon.

events.name: Mithridates I of Parthia conquers Mesopotamia
events.description: Mithridates I of Parthia takes Mesopotamia from the Seleucids and holds the Babylonian king as a captive, ending Seleucid rule in the east.

events.name: Battle of Carrhae
events.description: The Parthian army under Surena defeats Crassus and destroys seven legions of Rome in Mesopotamia.

events.name: Battle of Nisibis between Rome and Parthia
events.description: Vologases V defeats the Roman emperor Caracalla's successor Macrinus near Nisibis and secures terms for Parthia.

events.name: Ardashir I overthrows the Parthian Empire
events.description: Ardashir I defeats Artabanus V and founds the Sassanid dynasty, reviving Persian imperial rule from Ctesiphon.

events.name: Shapur I captures the Roman emperor Valerian
events.description: Shapur I defeats and captures Valerian at Edessa, an unprecedented humiliation for Rome, recorded in his own investiture inscriptions.

events.name: Heraclius defeats the Sassanids near Nineveh
events.description: Heraclius routs the Sassanid army near Nineveh, ending the last Byzantine–Sassanid war and restoring the pre-war borders.

events.name: Pompey reorganizes the Roman East
events.description: Pompey ends the Seleucid kingdom and reorganizes Syria and the client kingdoms, bringing Rome to the Mesopotamian frontier.

events.name: Trajan annexes Mesopotamia
events.description: Trajan captures Ctesiphon and briefly makes Mesopotamia a Roman province, the empire's furthest reach in the east.

events.name: Julian campaigns against the Sassanids
events.description: Julian advances to Ctesiphon and fights the Sassanid army before dying during the retreat from Mesopotamia.

events.name: Tiglath-Pileser III takes the throne of Babylon
events.description: Tiglath-Pileser III takes the Babylonian crown in addition to the Assyrian throne, binding Babylon closely to Assyria.

events.name: Esarhaddon begins the rebuilding of Babylon
events.description: Esarhaddon orders the restoration of Babylon after his father Sennacherib's destruction of the city.

events.name: Shamash-shum-ukin revolts against Ashurbanipal
events.description: The Assyrian-appointed Babylonian king Shamash-shum-ukin rebels against his brother Ashurbanipal, sparking a devastating civil war.
